briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 20, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Crisis, Alarms Ringing Worldwide: Extreme Weather Events and Their Aftermath
sections.content: Today, alarm bells signaling the severity of the climate crisis have rung out across the globe. In France, unprecedented heatwaves have triggered student protests [1], and in our nation's coastal waters, temperatures have risen significantly, making high-temperature phenomena commonplace [2, 6, 12, 18]. Notably, a new climate scenario has been announced in Vietnam, indicating that super typhoons could be experienced every seven years [21], while Panama's canal is being choked by severe drought, threatening the livelihoods of farmers [172]. Furthermore, a village in Norway has been unable to drink tap water for a year due to drinking water contamination caused by climate change [5], and damage across ecosystems is spreading, including the earlier emergence of pine wilt disease vectors [10]. The lawsuit filed by New York City against major energy corporations like ExxonMobil for climate change greenwashing [157] sends a crucial message regarding corporate responsibility.

sections.title: 🌱 Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Society: Domestic and International Policies, and Citizen Participation
sections.content: Efforts to transition to a carbon-neutral society in response to the climate crisis are also actively continuing. The European Union (EU) has demonstrated international leadership by proposing fossil fuel transition and greenhouse gas reduction as key agenda items for COP31 [15], and by supporting 77 carbon-neutral technology projects with 3.4 billion Euros [26, 32, 126]. Domestically, Namyangju City has opened a Carbon Neutrality Support Center, activating a policy implementation hub to achieve its goal of a 41.3% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 [11, 25, 34, 36, 37, 38, 39, 42, 73, 75], and the Mayor of Gwangmyeong City has proposed to the Minister of Climate that national support for local government carbon neutrality efforts be expanded [24, 35, 43, 44, 52, 58, 62, 64, 76]. Furthermore, various carbon neutrality initiatives involving citizens are spreading nationwide, such as the Chungbuk Provincial Office of Education operating programs where students experience the climate crisis with all five senses, and the Chungbuk Provincial Government hosting a Carbon Neutrality Culture Festival [13, 17, 19, 27, 28, 29, 33, 51, 53, 55, 57, 66, 72, 74, 87, 90, 95]. The participation of 440 individuals in Siheung City's vehicle carbon neutrality point system, with incentives scheduled for payment in December [22, 65, 69, 81, 84, 86, 92], is also interpreted as a positive sign of citizen engagement.

sections.title: ⚠️ The Light and Shadow of Renewable Energy Transition: Expansion Efforts and Current Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy faces several challenges despite continuous investment and effort. Investments in expanding renewable energy projects are continuing both domestically and internationally, with the Nakdong River Basin Environmental Office supporting 10 billion KRW for renewable energy expansion in the Gyeongnam and Gyeongbuk regions [99, 102, 109, 124], [101, 104, 120, 127]. Western Power is also planning to develop a 13MW solar power facility in the Daejeon Industrial Complex, intending to return generation profits to the local community [115, 116, 117, 128, 135, 144]. However, concerns have been raised that regional electricity pricing systems hinder renewable energy investments and signal a red light for new power generation projects [98], and there have been criticisms that regulations intended to expand renewable energy are actually impeding progress [118]. Notably, a National Assembly audit briefing indicated that with 113 trillion KRW needed for power grid expansion and Korea Electric Power Corporation's debt reaching 210 trillion KRW, discussions on electricity tariff increases are necessary [142]. Furthermore, regarding the power shortage issue in the Yongin Semiconductor Industrial Complex, arguments have been made for a project re-evaluation considering renewable energy supply capabilities [125], highlighting the urgent need for fundamental solutions to ensure a stable energy transition.

sections.title: 🌍 Climate Science and International Response: Research, Dialogue, and Responsibility
sections.content: Efforts to enhance scientific understanding of climate change and seek international cooperation are also ongoing. In California, the 5th Climate Change Assessment analyzed the impact of rising temperatures on Southern California [150, 154], and New Zealand has reported that its climate has entered 'uncharted territory' [161]. Domestically, Ewha Womans University hosted the International Cloud Experts Conference for the first time in Asia to discuss responses to the climate crisis [20]. In the international community, the Chair of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change visited Northern Ireland to conduct a fact-finding mission [148, 167, 170], and in Bucharest, 2,100 participants gathered for a climate change summit, announcing a rebranding for 2027 [162], indicating active discussions. Meanwhile, discussions are underway in the Supreme Court regarding who will bear the costs of climate change [165], and criticisms have been raised that some politicians' climate change denialism has reached a 'melting point' [164], signifying growing societal demands for accountability and improved awareness regarding the climate crisis.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the multifaceted aspects of the climate crisis, reiterating the importance of global cooperation and swift action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
